description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s incident history for a period with the disclosure summary it gives buyers: the history with the service, the period and each incident with its id, title, start and end times or minutes and cause; the disclosure with the service, the period, the incident count and total minutes it states and each incident it lists with the history incident it cites, its title, minutes and cause. The signed report gives the history and the disclosure, each disclosed incident matched to a history incident by the incident it cites and then by title, every history incident missing from the disclosure named, each duration and cause on each side, and the disclosure’s count and total against the history, and counts them, and names a misreported disclosure: an incident in the history missing from the disclosure, a duration shorter than the history records, another cause than the history records and a count or total below the history; then a disclosed incident not in the history, a longer duration, a cause left out, another title, a higher count or total and another period or service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. A history incident with no duration or no cause where the disclosure states one, or with no minutes where a total is stated, leaves the disclosure unverified. Durations compare to the tenth of a minute and causes and titles by their words. This reads a whole period against what buyers are told: wever_status-evidence-check reads one status page, as text or one public page read once, and lists the figures and entries it carries, and wever_incident-evidence-check reads one incident’s claims against the timeline and postmortem offered for that incident, while the incident history check reads no status page as its subject and reads a period’s full history against the summary disclosure given to buyers. Verdict rely_incident-history_misreported, rely_incident-history_partial, rely_incident-history_unverified or rely_incident-history_faithful. POST /api/rely-incident-history-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
